invoice-due-default: change the default due date for new invoices pick the number of days added to today for newly created invoices on this computer. invoices & payments invoice due date default payment terms days net 30 net 14 net 7 open company & settings → options for this computer. choose new invoice due date: same day, 7, 14, 30, 45 or 60 days. select save computer options. create a new invoice and review its actual invoice date and due date before saving. if you change the invoice date, review the due date too. existing invoices keep their previous dates. to correct one, open its details and use edit invoice when available. a new invoice proposes the selected due date. no old invoices change automatically.
sync-disabled: automatic sync is off — how do i turn it back on? switch it on in computer options, or use sync now yourself. office & devices auto sync disabled turn on sync sync interval no automatic reconnect on the affected laptop, open company & settings → options for this computer. set automatically reconnect and sync to on. choose check for changes every, then save computer options. open office & devices and select sync now to check immediately. if pending changes does not clear, read any connection or review message. turning automatic sync on does not resolve conflicting edits. the laptop checks the office at the selected interval while the app is running.
manual-code-fallback: use a long connection code when nearby discovery is unavailable the manual-code option remains available for networks that block discovery. office & devices long connection code paste invitation manual connection discovery blocked existing code on the host: office & devices → create device invitation. enter a name for this laptop, select its access role and review the office address. if several adapters are listed, use the address reachable from that laptop. create the code and transfer the complete text securely to the intended user. on the standalone laptop: office & devices → i already have a connection code. paste the entire long code and select connect. if the laptop says office host, follow the missing join guide first. if the host is unavailable, check its listener before generating more codes. the laptop loads the correct office records. only one device uses that invitation.
save-versus-sync: it says all changes saved — have they reached the office? saved on this laptop and synced to the office are different states. office & devices all changes saved saved but missing sync versus save pending zero last sync all changes saved means your form was saved to this computer. open office & devices and look at pending changes and last sync. when online, choose sync now. wait for pending changes to reach 0 and check for a review message. ask the office to open the same customer, bid or time entry. refresh their page if needed. if you are offline, keep the laptop and its backup safe. do not enter the same work on another computer just because the office cannot see it yet. the record is visible in the office workspace after a successful sync.
buttons-missing: a button is missing, grey, or unavailable on this computer available actions depend on the workspace and access role. everyday tasks button missing grey button cannot approve cannot edit not available read only check whether the demo banner is shown. return to your company for office setup and company work. in office & devices, check this computer’s role. field laptops create customers, bids and draft time; office financial changes belong at the host or connected office workstation. a paid invoice, issued bid or approved time entry may be locked or use a special correction workflow. search that item in help. if the office workstation is offline, restore its connection before saving financial changes. for a missing join button specifically, follow only create device invitation appears. you can identify whether the action is limited by role, record status, or connection.
paid-wages-double-count: employee wages seem to be counted twice approved employee time already creates a linked labor expense. employees & time wages twice duplicate labor double payroll employee expense duplicate time cost twice open employees & time and find the employee and date. approved time creates its labor expense automatically. recording its wage settlement marks that linked expense paid; it does not need a second general expense. open expenses & income and look for a separate manually entered expense for the same hours. if you confirm a manual duplicate, back up first, then remove only that duplicate. keep the expense linked to the time entry. track employer taxes, benefits or other extra costs separately only if they are not already included in the rate used for those hours. the job contains one labor cost for the approved time, and cash reflects its recorded payment once.
month-is-empty: this month is empty even though i entered work different screens use different dates and payment states. everyday tasks empty month zero monthly total graph blank wrong month missing monthly income open company & settings and check reporting year. for cash received, confirm you recorded an invoice payment or other income with a date in that month. creating an invoice alone is not money received. for cash spent, confirm the expense is marked paid and check date paid. an unpaid bill still counts as a cost but not cash spent. for labor, draft hours have not yet created job costs. an authorized office user must review and approve them. check the wording under each total: some show all dates while charts use the reporting year. the total agrees with the transactions and dates included by that screen.
profit-review-start: open profit review from reports find job-margin, billing, collection and missing-data flags in one place. profit review leak leakage profit review money losing business leak detector bonus action list where is bonus bonus missing moved profit review reports choose profit review near the top of the left menu. its bonus feature badge disappears after first opening and stays dismissed on this computer. high priority means a projected job loss or an invoice more than 30 days late. other flags ask you to check a situation; they do not prove money was lost. use the search box for a job, customer, invoice or issue. choose a group to narrow the list. open show calculation & limits to see the exact basis. use the next-step button to open the source record. the page shows up to 100 matching flags. narrow the search to find others. save full review pdf exports all flags, including ones outside the current filter. review all dates and missing records. no flags does not mean your records are complete. you can explain a flag from its underlying job, invoice or time record.
profit-review-margin: why a job is below target or projected to lose money job profit is approved contract value minus recorded job costs and remaining costs with contingency. profit review leak margin why profit dropped target gap loss extra price remaining costs open the job flag and expand show calculation & limits. projected loss means the forecast final cost exceeds the contract. positive profit below the target margin is not a loss. price gap assumes costs stay unchanged. the alternative cost gap assumes price stays unchanged. do not add the two amounts or treat them as guaranteed savings. do not invoice the gap automatically. obtain customer approval for extra scope and include its extra costs in your forecast. job forecasts do not allocate separately recorded company overhead. employee time contributes gross wages once approved; add extra employer costs separately when applicable. the contract less forecast cost equals the displayed job profit.
profit-review-billing: unbilled work, overdue invoices and submitted changes these three flags have different meanings and are not extra profit to add together. profit review unbilled invoice now retention deposit overdue invoice submitted extra unbilled is approved contract less issued invoices, before tax. future work, deposits and retention may have special billing terms. review milestones first. overdue is an invoice balance including tax that remains after its due date. check whether the customer has already paid before sending a reminder. open review invoice to see payments or copy a reminder. nothing is emailed automatically. submitted change value is excluded from the contract until approved. draft and rejected changes are excluded. archived jobs can still have overdue invoice flags because archiving does not settle a balance. unbilled amounts are before tax; overdue balances include invoice tax and deduct recorded payments.
profit-review-data: draft hours and missing or outdated forecasts incomplete information can make profit look better or worse than it really is. profit review draft time pending employee hours forecast missing cost changed double counting remaining stale forecast blank future costs means the forecast is incomplete. enter only the costs still to come; enter 0 only when none remain. a cost or approved change saved after the job can trigger a reminder. payment-status edits can trigger it too; review the facts. when you record a cost, remove that work from future costs. the app does not reduce the remaining estimate automatically. draft time is excluded from actual job costs. review employee hours and approve them at the office; a linked expense then posts once. do not enter the same wages again manually. profit review includes draft hours across all dates. search by job or employee in employees & time to review each record. completed jobs assume no future costs. change the status if work and costs are still outstanding. remaining costs exclude work already recorded, and approved hours have exactly one linked expense.
profit-review-estimate: understand category overruns and missing baselines the category comparison uses the original accepted estimate, not an updated detailed budget. profit review estimate actual category overrun materials labor fuel no baseline budget variance open show calculation & limits on a category flag to compare original estimated cost, recorded cost and the difference. recorded cost exceeding a nonzero original category amount triggers a comparison. it is not a second loss to add to the overall job forecast. approved changes and estimate overhead can be unallocated. check whether new scope explains the extra cost. a category with no original amount is labeled missing a baseline, not assumed to be a zero-cost plan. a manually created job without an accepted estimate can still use its total cost budget, but cannot establish category overruns. for future jobs, build the estimate with the relevant materials, labor, equipment and other categories before accepting it. you know which baseline is being compared and which scope or costs it leaves out.
profit-review-sync: why a laptop profit review differs from the office each computer reviews its currently saved copy of the records. profit review leak sync review offline different totals outdated office review missing field hours read connection & data freshness at the top of profit review. an offline laptop may be missing office changes. open office & devices and sync. resolve any displayed conflict before relying on totals. ask every field laptop to reconnect and sync its bids and draft time. the office cannot see work that remains offline on another laptop. after syncing, the office still needs to review and approve draft hours before they become actual job costs. the review refreshes when saved records change and you are not editing. it never overwrites an open form just to refresh an alert. all relevant devices have synced and any draft hours or missing expenses have been reviewed.
profit-review-planning: overhead increases and cash-buffer flags planning flags describe saved expenses and a manually entered cash scenario. profit review overhead rose cash buffer cash shortfall safe to spend plan outdated overhead compares the last two complete calendar months by expense date. paid and unpaid company costs are included; job costs are excluded. a rise of at least 10% is flagged only when the earlier month had recorded overhead. review one-off spending and missing bills before concluding there is a trend. the cash alert finds the first current or future week below your buffer in the saved receipts-shortfall scenario. the cash plan is manual. it does not read a bank balance or automatically import bills, payroll or invoices. update the inputs before relying on it. an expired plan is flagged for updating instead of showing old shortfalls as current. the dates and assumptions match the decision you are making.
